title: Building nuclei: isotopes and nuclear notation
description: Protons and neutrons, atomic and mass number, nuclear notation and isotopes with the Isotope Builder, and the short-range strong force that holds the nucleus together against the repulsion of its protons.

sources.title: Atomic nucleus (Wikipedia): Rutherford 1911, R = r0·A^(1/3), nucleus about 1/60 000 (hydrogen) to 1/27 000 (uranium) of the atom's diameter
Proton (Wikipedia): Rutherford's identification 1917–1920, the name 'proton' 1920, mass about 1836 electron masses
The Nobel Prize in Physics 1935: James Chadwick, for the discovery of the neutron
James Chadwick (Wikipedia): 1891–1974, Cavendish Laboratory, letter 'Possible Existence of a Neutron' to Nature, February 1932, polonium–beryllium radiation on paraffin
Isotope (Wikipedia): the word suggested by Margaret Todd to Frederick Soddy in 1913, Greek 'same place'; about 251 stable nuclides
Nuclear force (Wikipedia): attractive from about 0.7 fm, negligible beyond about 2.5 fm, repulsive core below 0.7 fm, nearly the same for protons and neutrons
Deuterium (Wikipedia): about 1 in 6420 hydrogen atoms (0.0156 %), discovered by Harold Urey in 1931
NUBASE2020 and AME2020 (IAEA Atomic Mass Data Center): stability, half-lives (tritium 12.3 a, carbon-14 5700 a) and masses in the Isotope Builder's data file
CODATA 2018 recommended values (NIST): proton, neutron and electron masses, e, u
